rationale: The two buttons are paired screen-reader labels on the same toolbar ("Navigate back"/"Navigate forward"); they should share the same verbal form for consistency.
summary: Forward-navigation content description uses a noun ("Перехід уперед") while its paired back-navigation string uses an imperative verb ("Перейти назад").

rationale: Ukrainian punctuation requires a comma to set off a дієприслівниковий зворот; without it the sentence is grammatically mis-punctuated.
summary: Missing comma before the participial phrase "перейшовши до…".

rationale: In English, "About" works on its own as a menu label. In Ukrainian, "Про" needs an object (for example "Про програму"). On its own it is ungrammatical.
summary: The menu item is the bare preposition "Про" with no object, so it reads as unfinished.

rationale: The en-US sentence ends with a period before </label>. The Ukrainian leaves it out, although the first sentence in the same string keeps its period.
summary: The final sentence has lost the full stop that ends the source sentence.

rationale: The source and the developer comment both refer to the user's own list of URLs. "Популярних сайтів" mixes this up with the separate built-in list of 450 popular URLs (preference_autocomplete_topsite_summary2), so it misdescribes what the toggle does.
summary: "Your favorite URLs" (the list the user builds) is translated as "URLs of popular sites".

rationale: The source names a mode that allows only HTTPS connections. "HTTPS-режим" just means "HTTPS mode" and loses the restriction. Firefox uses "Режим лише HTTPS" for this.
summary: "HTTPS-Only Mode" is rendered as "HTTPS-режим", which drops the "only" meaning.

rationale: "Дотики і прокручування" are examples of the activity being measured ("вимірювання активності"), so they need the same genitive case.
summary: The example nouns are in the nominative case but should agree with the genitive "активності".
